answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each participant to lock a scarce token as a bond before earning reputation or receiving payments. A newcomer’s bond stays at risk during a challenge window: if peers prove that several identities share the same controller, the system slashes those bonds and redistributes them to honest reporters. The whisper of a river may hide many names, but each fake identity still ties up capital and risks a pearl-sized loss; scaling the attack therefore becomes costly rather than free.
